To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the response of maize to fertilizer was adversely affected by high levels of precipitation, but that the response was not affected by low levels of precipitation.
the maize grain yield response and profitability are adversely affected by increased level of precipitation and the fertilizer requirements for maize production are affected by the rainfall level.

the development of an economic model for fertilizer use in maize production.
the development and use of a predictive equation relating grain yield of maize (Zea mays L.) to fertilizer application and rainfall.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
maize yield responses to N and P were highly variable, and the profitability of N and P applications were affected by precipitation.

rainfall has a significant effect on fertilizer response and fertilizer requirements for maximum profitability.
